items.tx:
WOW WOW WOW

Some unbelievable heavy artillery being exchanged between the majority and the dissenters here. 

An en banc decision from a 17 judge court, with a 10-7 split, we get a majority opinion, three concurring opinions, and two dissenting opinions.

Combined they total 157 pages. 

FAR too much to dissect today.

BUT, this cases raise the sole issue that was remaining on detaining illegal aliens caught in the country will removal proceedings are conducted -- whether the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment requires that they be given a bond hearing even if the statutory language used by Congress specified otherwise. 

The cases SCOTUS has agreed to take up involve only what the statute's require in terms of a bail hearing -- not whether due process requires one even if the statutes do not. 

But some Judges granting bail hearings have entered alternative rulings when ordering the release of aliens while removal proceedings are underway. Their orders state that even if they are wrong on what the statute requires, the 5th Amendment Due Process clause requires a hearing before liberty can be deprived for such aliens.

This en banc decision by the Fifth Circuit raises the issue -- which the SCOTUS could now decide to take up at the same time it is going to the statutory cases.
